$comment: What each CLI can actually prove about its own lifecycle. Read by TypeScript (fidelity.ts) and by Rust (agent_life.rs, include_str!) so the two can never drift. Every event name here is asserted by src/agentFidelityGuard.test.ts to appear literally inside that CLI's setup_* function in src-tauri/src/agents.rs, and vice versa: a plugin template that renames an event fails CI instead of silently freezing that CLI's state forever. Do not hand-edit a row without re-reading the installer and bumping verifiedAt.

clis.$note: The only CLI whose own completion notice is distinguishable from a permission request by text it authors itself. promptReadyText is consulted only because notification is "mixed".

PermissionRequest is its own event, so blocked is structural and no text is read. unstampedBus: the legacy notify line (agents.rs setup_codex_notify) appends to the bus with no canopy_pty stamp. needsTrust: hooks are written but inert until the user runs /hooks.

agy's hook stdin carries no message field and the helper is registered without --message, so nothing in a Notification can be read. Declared unmapped rather than guessed: before this manifest every agy notification returned "waiting" and the session stayed pinned there until its next PostInvocation. Flip this to "block" the day agy's payload is verified.

One integration total: notifications-command, which aider runs both after a turn and at a y/n confirm. It wants the keyboard and cannot say which kind. Classified attention-only, never "finished" — idle is what auto-hibernation SIGTERMs and what the folded Idle stack hides, and the two failure directions are not symmetric.
The permission signal arrives on its own bus event. It used to be re-encoded as prose and re-parsed, which let a tool-supplied title containing "waiting for" convert a block into "finished".
Registered through try/catch against an API its own installer calls "in flux": a rename registers nothing and throws nothing. The guard test over these names is the only thing that would notice.

No notification event of any kind, so "blocked on you" is structurally unprovable for amp. An amp session parked on an approval prompt used to read "working" indefinitely; it now decays to unknown rather than being fabricated into waiting.
